correctness.rationale: The theorem has universal quantifiers \(m,n\ge1\) and every prescribed T. Necessity uses parity of the indegree sum and the DAG source. Under these conditions the possible-sink count q is positive by the four parity cases. In the safe-source lemma, after deleting an A source the new source count is \(a-1+n-b\) and the possible-sink count is q minus 1 exactly when n is even; symmetric expressions hold for B. The \(q\ge2\) case chooses a deletion retaining a source. In the \(q=1\) case, both-even contradicts global parity, both-odd preserves q, and the mixed cases force a safe source in the odd-degree side. A removed source toggles exactly its neighbors, preserving the global parity equation; the star base case is explicit. Hence the induction and signature counting work for all positive m,n. Replayed artifacts/verify.py independently enumerates each edge orientation for \(1\le m,n\le4\) and verifies the constructive claim for 4032 canonical profiles, \(1\le m,n\le12\). Finite checks are evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Same graph family and same prescribed-parity quantity were searched in published mathematical records and primary literature. West 1995 treats the number of independent (freely reversible) edges of acyclic \(K_{m,n}\) orientations and offers an alternating-block representation, not the image of the vertex indegree-parity map. Gravier et al. 2026 introduces the parity-restricted acyclic-orientation problem and catalogs necessary conditions and Cartesian-product families; indexed material does not show a \(K_{m,n}\) classification. Its full text could not be read, so this remains a named priority risk, not a claimed certified absence. Structural acyclic-bitournament characterizations do not state the universal target-wise parity image. Search matches about non-separating out-branchings concern a different orientation property.

value.rationale: A natural two-parameter infinite family of bicliques is completely classified for every labelled prescribed indegree parity target, a problem posed in recent orientation research. The source obstruction is proved to be the only one beyond edge parity, with the exact parity-dependent unique exceptional all-odd target and an \(O((m+n)^2+mn)\) constructive procedure. This is a structural family classification and not merely a textbook parity identity: the nontrivial safe-source reduction maintains acyclicity and needed source/sink witnesses across the recursion.
